title: 2023 - Year in Review - Channel Update / Patron Q&A / Best Gaming Experiences of the Year
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eu92DDq5snw

Daniel (@dungeondive) opens by asking viewers to be kind to themselves, then explains why: 2023 brought cognitive decline from long covid that he doesn't expect to fully recover from, and the deaths of his father-in-law, an old friend, and his dog. He still produced over 150 videos, and describes escaping into tabletop games as genuinely therapeutic.

The channel update is frank. Views have never recovered from something that happened around October 2022, YouTube isn't paying the bills, and he gives it one more year at this level while shifting weight to Patreon. The response is a deliberate slowdown — fewer videos, roughly two a week, each covering fewer games in more depth. He is not burned out on playing games, but on constantly learning new ones at the expense of the ones he loves.

The patron Q&A surfaces League of Dungeoneers and 2d6 Dungeon as community favourites. His own categories run wide: the Runebound Retrospective as his proudest series and his most frustrating reception; The Doomed for innovation; Doom Pilgrim as best small game; Albion's Legacy (deluxe) as the out-of-nowhere discovery; and HeroQuest with the fan-made Axian Quest cards, which he rates among the best expansions he's played for anything. Game of the year: Freelancers.

----

Is "fewer games, more deeply" a creative choice or a survival strategy — and can a channel do it and still be found?
